description: Add idempotency-key deduplication with a TTL window to a processor that currently re-executes on every call
prompts: processor.py's Processor.process(key, payload, now) runs the side effect (appends to self.effects and returns a fresh result) EVERY time it's called, even for a key it has already processed. Make it idempotent: within `window` seconds of the first call for a given key, a repeat call with that SAME key must return the ORIGINAL result WITHOUT running the side effect again (self.effects must not grow) - regardless of what payload is passed the second time. Once `window` seconds have passed since the first call for that key, the NEXT call for that key must run for real again (a fresh execution, whose result becomes the new one remembered for that key).

test_setup_files.test_processor_hidden.py:
from processor import Processor


def test_duplicate_key_within_window_is_not_reexecuted():
    p = Processor(window=10)
    first = p.process('order-1', {'amount': 5}, now=0)
    second = p.process('order-1', {'amount': 999}, now=5)
    assert second == first
    assert p.effects == [('order-1', {'amount': 5})]


def test_different_keys_both_execute():
    p = Processor(window=10)
    p.process('a', 1, now=0)
    p.process('b', 2, now=0)
    assert len(p.effects) == 2


def test_reexecutes_after_window_expires():
    p = Processor(window=10)
    p.process('order-1', {'amount': 5}, now=0)
    p.process('order-1', {'amount': 5}, now=9)
    assert len(p.effects) == 1
    p.process('order-1', {'amount': 7}, now=10)
    assert len(p.effects) == 2
    assert p.effects[-1] == ('order-1', {'amount': 7})
